results.question: How can legacy pods without an Istio sidecar connect to a STRICT mTLS service?
results.answer: When an Istio namespace or workload is configured with `PeerAuthentication` in `STRICT` mode, any client connecting over plain unencrypted TCP/HTTP without an authenticated mTLS certificate handshake will be immediately rejected with TCP connection reset or `connection termination`. results.answer: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout occurs when an edge proxy or Kubernetes Ingress Controller (Nginx Ingress, AWS Load Balancer Controller / ALB, Traefik) fails to receive a timely response from an upstream backend service pod within the configured timeout window [kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md#kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md-c0] Heavy database queries, slow external API calls, or garbage collection pauses exceed the default 60-second Nginx `proxy-read-timeout`. - **Immediate Fix:** Add timeout annotations to the Ingress resource: ```yaml metadata: annotations: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout: "15" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "180" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "180" ``` For AWS ALB Ingress: ```yaml metadata: annotations: alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-attributes: idle_timeout.timeout_seconds=180 [kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md#kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md-c6] Client sees:** `504 Gateway Time-out` - **Ingress Controller log shows:** `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream` - **Impact:** Failed API transactions, degraded user checkout/request flows, and customer-facing incident alerts. results.question: How can site reliability engineers execute ad-hoc diagnostic commands inside a running container that lacks a shell?
results.answer: If the {{< glossary_tooltip text="container image" term_id="image" >}} includes debugging utilities, as is the case with images built from Linux and Windows OS base images, you can run commands inside a specific container with `kubectl exec`: ```shell kubectl exec ${POD_NAME} -c ${CONTAINER_NAME} -- ${CMD} ${ARG1} ${ARG2} ... ${ARGN} ``` {{< note >}} `-c ${CONTAINER_NAME}` is optional [debug-running-pod.md#debug-running-pod.md-c6] {{< /note >}} As an example, to look at the logs from a running Cassandra pod, you might run ```shell kubectl exec cassandra -- cat /var/log/cassandra/system.log ``` You can run a shell that's connected to your terminal using the `-i` and `-t` arguments to `kubectl exec`, for example: ```shell kubectl exec -it cassandra -- sh ``` For more details, see [Get a Shell to a Running Container]( /docs/tasks/debug/debug-application/get-shell-running-container/).
